hypothesis: Materializing frozen landing pointers avoids repeated full payload scans without changing code queries, candidates, ranking or provenance.

method.source: The canonical GitHub archive is opened read-only. Construction verifies repository and the frozen selected-observation digest.
method.index: SQLite WITHOUT ROWID table keyed by exact SHA and PR number, retaining observation ID, payload digest, field pointer and relation.
method.selection: The frozen latest observation per family and subject is selected before completeness filtering. Existing pull-git preference is preserved per SHA/PR pair; unmerged merge_commit_sha and PR membership alone are not landings.
method.attestation: New output paths only; publication metadata is written after construction. Opening validates schema, scope, complete ordered-row digest and SQLite integrity. An attested index must remain unchanged while in use.
method.lookup: B-tree lookup by exact SHA, then primary-key canonical observation lookup, frozen latest-subject verification, payload SHA-256 verification and exact field-pointer checks for each hit.
method.cost_boundary: Full row attestation is an open-time cost; lookup can reuse attested connections. Fresh read_landings calls include attestation. Later GitHub publications do not change the registered cutoff.
method.integration: future_search, entity_search and import_paths accept --landing-index. Omission retains the scanning control. Code relationships and traversal remain in CBM.

gates.pipeline_digest_rule: sha256(json.dumps(result, sort_keys=True).encode()) after removing run seconds and the relevant per-case or generated seconds; all query responses, candidates and evidence remain
synthetic_gates: Latest partial or unavailable observations do not restore older complete facts; independent family fallback remains explicit
Publication cutoff, observation-window ordering and ID ties
Unmerged targets, duplicate-source preference, multiple PRs per SHA and multiple SHAs per PR
Deleted or corrupted index rows, incomplete builds, corrupted source bytes and invalid source pointers
Wrong index or canonical repository, stale source selection and read-only source operation
Existing-output preservation, empty queries, exact bound SQL targets and queries across the 400-SHA chunk boundary
Native SQLite query plans use the SHA primary key and the canonical subject index

cost.control_selection: Smallest, median and largest nonempty recorded query sets; two repetitions with alternating scan/index order
cost.interpretation: The lookup-only process performs no full scan or graph projection. Pipeline runs still include CBM projection and Git history work. Page caches were not cleared and other work ran concurrently; these are component measurements, not a statistical end-to-end latency claim.

limitations: The index is complete for the selected eligible observations, not for all GitHub activity or all repository history. Empty matches do not establish absence from GitHub.
Attestation is linear in derived-index rows at open time. Construction still performs the full frozen selection and payload scan.
A new evidence cutoff requires a new index. No incremental maintenance or production query-service interface is introduced.
Exact landing evidence is not a causal-fix claim. The rejected R005 default and the R004 native include-coverage defect are unchanged.
Real effectiveness remains measured on one repository. Synthetic tests check generic source and SQL semantics, not cross-repository retrieval quality.

next.hypothesis: Diagnostic source spans and native CBM node kinds can prevent incidental path-to-symbol matches from consuming the retrieval budget, while retaining genuinely useful entity evidence.
next.controls: Keep the original diagnostic-name lane, lexical control and raw stack-path controls. Compare identical candidate budgets and retain uncertain bindings explicitly.
next.scope: Use the indexed landing backend without changing its semantics. Add generic synthetic noise and ambiguity cases; select further development inputs from the frozen hash-ordered pool before new retrieval runs.
next.gates: No repository-specific vocabulary exceptions, no gold-PR query inputs, exact source spans and graph predicates, retained useful development evidence, and explicit false-binding review. R005 cases are known diagnostic cases, not an untouched held-out test.
next.context_followup: Terminal-frame-only retrieval misses caller-side changes; contextual stack evidence remains a required subsequent relevance experiment, not solved by the landing index.
